Rosalie Spitzer Interment – Wed. 10:30 June 29, 2011

Welcome, my name is Terry. I’m one of the staff at Cropo. Thank you for being here today. We’ve come together to say goodbye to Rosalie and to leave her here in her final resting place on earth.

From what I understand, Rosalie was a fine lady, generous, non-complaining, and well liked. I know Allan and the rest of you here have helped her in so many different ways over the years. I’m told Rosalie was always very grateful for all your help. If she could speak here today, I’m sure she would again thank each of you for all you did for her.

Rosalie’s daughter Donna in B.C. was not able to be here today, but sent flowers and asked me to read a poem that she sent for this occasion. I’m going to give each of you a copy so that you can follow along as I read.

 

Always remembered, always loved.

As we go thru life, each of us have and will face many different challenges and difficult times. And no doubt, Rosalie had her share of challenges and difficult times too. And it’s at times like this when we appreciate the love, support and encouragement from family and friends. Again she would say thankyou.

I’m told that Rosalie kept a bible in her home for many years. Many of us in our difficult times often feel the need to go beyond our friends and family for help and look to God for encouragement, peace and strength. I believe each of us can connect with and feel God in different ways. It may be in nature, it may be in music, in silence, in certain people, in the bible, or in other ways. For Rosalie, it may have even been in the peace and beauty of her flower gardens that she felt God’s presence and comfort.

I understand that Rosalie wouldn’t be the type to like a lot of fuss or ceremony for herself, but as we gather here today, I know that each of you will have your very own special memories of Rosalie. And out of respect we’d like to honor her today by taking just a few moments of silence where I’d like you to consider a few things, “What did you like about Rosalie?”  Are there things you can learn from her that can make you a better person?”  Are there things you would like to say to her today, maybe goodbye, or thank you, or I forgive you, or I love you, or I’ll miss you, or perhaps you’d like to simply say a little prayer for her. Let’s take just a few moments of silence, and then I will end with a short prayer.

Thank you dear God for the life of Rosalie and the things we can learn from her. Thank you for all those that cared for her so well. We pray for Donna in B.C. and each one that cared for Rosalie here in Winnipeg too. Please give them all comfort, hope and strength for the days that lie ahead. As we lay Rosalie to rest here today we pray for her soul and commit her remains to the earth. May you bless and keep her, and may she rest in peace. Amen
